newsitem.title: POLAND: Six investors eye stake in Polish Ruch newsstand.
newsitem.headline: Six investors eye stake in Polish Ruch newsstand.

text.p: Six investors showed initial interest in purchasing at least 10 percent of Poland's largest newsstand chain Ruch SA, the treasury ministry's privatisation consultant said on Wednesday.

"Six applications (for Ruch) were placed," Krzysztof Wiater from the Law Offices of Furtek, Palinka and Zielinski told Reuters, but declined to say if the French Hachette consortium was among the six potential investors.

Hachette had signed an initial agreement with the ministry late last year on a purchase of 75 percent of Ruch but lost exclusive rights after it failed to meet the ministry's demand to present an improved offer.
Wiater said that potential investors had until April 18 to place their initial bids.
In March the ministry again opened a tender for Ruch, which owns 17,000 kiosks nationwide and controls 65 percent of Poland's press distribution market.
Last week the Universal SA led Polish Capital Group (PGK) said it had placed a bid for Ruch.
